title: Experimental observation of entropic-singularity-induced nonadditive quantum communication in a qutrit platypus channel
summary: The nonadditivity of channel capacity is a defining feature that distinguishes quantum communication from classical communication. In the quantum realm, the channel capacity is determined by coherent information, which is defined through the von Neumann entropies of the output and its environment. Despite its fundamental importance, experimental evidence of such nonadditive quantum communication has been elusive because of the complexity of the required quantum channel. Here, we experimentally observe entropic-singularity-induced coherent-information nonadditivity using the qutrit platypus…
